column1: Feed your starter ahead of time so it is bubbly, active, and roughly doubled in size.
Stir the starter and warm water together in a large bowl. Add both flours and the salt, then mix until no dry flour remains. The dough will look rough and shaggy.
Cover and rest the dough for 30 minutes.
Stretch one side of the dough up and fold it over the center. Rotate the bowl and repeat on all four sides. Complete 3 sets, spacing them about 30 minutes apart.

Cover and leave the dough in a warm place until noticeably larger, airy, and slightly domed, with bubbles and a soft, slightly jiggly texture. Aim for a 50–75% increase in volume; this may take 4–8 hours depending on temperature and starter strength.

Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and gently fold the edges toward the center to make a rough ball. Flip seam-side down and use cupped hands to rotate and tighten the dough until its surface is smooth and slightly taut.
Let the dough rest for 15–20 minutes, then shape it again into a tight round loaf.
Set the dough seam-side up in a lightly floured proofing basket or a bowl lined with a floured towel. Cover and refrigerate for 8–16 hours.
Place a Dutch oven in the oven and preheat to 450°F (232°C) for 30–45 minutes.
Turn the cold dough onto parchment paper. Score the top with one confident slash about 1/4 inch (6 mm) deep.
Carefully place the dough in the hot Dutch oven, cover, and bake at 450°F (232°C) for 25–30 minutes.
Remove the lid and bake for another 15–20 minutes, until the crust is deeply golden brown.
Transfer the loaf to a wire rack and cool for at least 1–2 hours before slicing.
